text: On QNX 8.0, all 17 tests named by the changes pass with the port; the unchanged release fails 15. An independent client passes 8 of 8.
open62541 compiles for QNX, but has no test system there. This project checks that it behaves as on Linux.
Each test runs twice on QNX, release and port. A change stays only where its tests show a difference: 17 named tests in all.
One command on a Windows PC builds, boots QNX in QEMU, runs the tests and writes the report. No board needed.
This is the raw QNX console: one line per test. The report is made from these lines only.
15 tests fail with the unchanged release and pass with the port. Red is fail, green is pass, grey could not run.
A probe without open62541 measures the operating system: 43 of 96 behaviours differ from Linux. The changes are built on these.
The whole suite: 80 pass and 2 fail with the port, 57 and 17 with the release. The two failures happen in both builds.
A Python client on the host logs in to the QNX server, encrypted. A wrong password and an unknown certificate are refused.
The demo server publishes CPU load, memory, processes and uptime every second, and logs to slog2.
open62541-qnx is open source. Under emulation, these are behaviour results, not performance figures.
